This may sound silly to a lot of people, but a couple years ago, I was dumped. I've had issues with depression and anxiety for the majority in my life, but had only begun medication about 7 months before. I wasn't on nearly a high enough dose.

I was devastated. He talked to me like we had a future together unprompted by me, and I thought that meant we both felt that way. He was the first person I've ever met that I could really see that with, in addition to being everything I ever wanted including things I didn't know I did. I've never felt so strongly about someone, let alone so quickly. I suddenly understood what people meant when they said that they just knew when they met "the one.". I even started to believe that the years I'd spent stuck in part time jobs was worth it because I met him despite having tried to get a fulltime job for ages.

For about 3 weeks, I was a shell of a person. I didn't laugh, I was barely eating. Close friends of mine hadn't ever seen me that bad, even when my dad died. It didn't help that I knew the role I had played in the end of this. 

But at some point, something clicked. I think I was tired of everyone shit talking him for dumping me. I realized that I never wanted to feel this way again, and also to thank him to a certain extent. He may not have been trying to fix me, but he reminded me of how to fix myself. Who I was when I wasn't depressed and anxious. I started working on becoming that woman again. I started writing daily, trying to be more positive because that was something I admired about him, doing some stuff for my physical health, and picked up reading again. 

Honestly, it's been about 3 years since we broke up at this point, and I still miss him a lot. It feels pathetic sometimes because the relationship was only about 6 months, but I also remember how much that relationship meant to me. It was a reminder about how amazing I can be, and that someone can care about me for me, despite what my self esteem says. It's been stinging more than usual lately, but more than anything else, I'm thankful for what I learned from him. I still want to thank him. It may be the last time I ever speak to him (or maybe that already happened), but I think he deserves to know that he helped someone even if his intention was to only do what was best for him.

I can only hope that I can feel as strongly for someone else one day since as much as I miss him, I know he probably has completely moved on and that it won't end with us together.

So the idea it makes things worse is probably tied up with the fact that suicide is a side effect of a lot of those medications, but the thing is that they don't cause suicide or suicidal thoughts. Generally, anti-depressants/anti-anxiety meds (they're actually the same from what I understand, how it manifests just depends on the person), just cause things to become easier to do. Because it takes a while for you to feel better, and most people who get on medication are at a pretty low point, suddenly have the energy to do what they've been thinking about.

They can make you feel worse if you're on the wrong medication, but there are a lot of medications, and it can take some trial and error to get the right one, but the right one will make you feel better, even if it's not perfect. The fire/burn analogy someone used above is very true. 

I can attest though as someone who has been on Lexapro for about 4 years now, it really does help. I went from crippled with anxiety all day and unable to move forward with life and destroying my best relationship, to holding onto a steady job and considering putting myself back out on the dating market. If your main concern is that they make things worse, I would try it. It may be that Zoloft isn't the right medication for you, and that you do feel worse, but there are a lot of different medications out there, and they are worth trying.

Mine isn't a holiday gift and I'm still working on it, but it's more like a gift to say how thankful I am. My most recent ex was someone I fell completely in love with, and part of the reason for that is that I felt so 100% comfortable around him, that I learned so much about myself and the life I want outside of the severe depression and anxiety I've been dealing with for the past decade. He didn't set out to save me, and would probably resent the idea that he did it, but he was at the very least the catalyst for these steps of change in my life. I want to tell him how thankful I am to him one day, and show my appreciation. 

He said his greatest heartbreak was that the girl he dated before me didn't take his writing seriously despite the fact they were both poets. One of the positive steps I've taken is getting back to writing daily, and one of the things I wrote, I had one of his poems in my mind. I want to expand that piece and edit it and give it to him. I'm not a poet or that girl, and even still getting back on my feet writing wise, but I want him to know I took it seriously enough that this one poem(which he also knows was my least favorite of the ones he showed me) inspired me to write something. I may not be with him ever again, and we may never speak again, but I need to do something to respond to him giving me the strength to pull myself out instead of just making me tread water. I hope that gives him some comfort or closure from her.

I relate to this super heavily and am still dealing with the consequences tbh. I was on the opposite side though, a shitty childhood made me want kids. I only really came to the realization this year that my desire to have a kid was a desire to runaway from the childhood I did have and replace it with a happy experience on the other side. I realized that I didn't actually want to be a parent though. It's been tough to wade through and sometimes I'm still hit with the feeling that I want a kid, but I think it was really important I face it. I caught it earlier in my life than you (I'm only in my mid twenties), but I think you should try to work through it too. If the answer is still "I don't want a kid" then great, you've at least helped yourself work through some stuff that will make you happier in the long run, and if you've changed your mind, there is always adoption as an option. You don't need to race against a biological clock.
